baseline.driver_probe: Failed during secure-app region notification: SMC function 0x32000105 returned raw -8; SCM return registers were zero; qseecom reported send secapp reg fail -22 and platform probe failed -22.

variant.method: one-time fastboot boot; no partition flashed
variant.only_dtb_change: Added qcom,appsbl-qseecom-support to /soc/qcom,qseecom@6500000. Semantic DTB comparison found no other property changes.
variant.result: QSEECOM platform device bound to driver qseecom; /dev/qseecom created (major 240, minor 0). The prior app-region notification failure path was skipped. qseecomd ran and sys.listeners.registered=true.

follow_up.credential_bound_KeyInfo: Not rerun. The Android user was RUNNING_LOCKED after boot, so the diagnostic activity could not launch. Temporary APK was uninstalled.
follow_up.iris_unlock_readiness: Still unproven. QSEE device binding does not establish that Android Keymaster selects a TEE-backed key implementation or that secure-hardware credential enforcement works.
follow_up.return_to_installed_kernel: Rebooted normally after the temporary boot. Kernel #18 is running again and /dev/qseecom is absent, confirming the DT variant was temporary.

cleanup.camera_clients: none observed; no camera trace errors

UEFI_memory_map_lead.entry: 0x06500000, 0x00500000, TZ Apps, reserved non-secure device memory
UEFI_memory_map_lead.interpretation: This matches the Linux QSEE app-region range exactly and supports a bootloader-managed QSEE memory-region hypothesis. It does not prove that UEFI issued QSEE's app-region notification.
